title: 걷기 좋은 동네, 부모님이 더 걸으시는 길의 조건
description: 걷기 좋은 동네에 사는 어르신은 신체활동이 더 많았다는 연구가 많았어요. 보행로와 보기 좋은 거리가 몸 기능과 관련이 있었다는 연구로 부모님 동네 산책길을 살펴봐요.
image_alt: 걷기 좋은 동네 골목길, 화분이 놓인 길을 따라 장바구니를 들고 집으로 걸어가는 할머니를 그린 수채화
image_prompt: Soft watercolor illustration of an elderly Korean woman walking home along a quiet autumn alley lined with flower pots, carrying a shopping bag with vegetables. No writing, letters or numbers.
body_markdown:
명절에 부모님 댁에 갔다가 같이 장을 보러 나섰는데, 가는 길에 인도가 끊기고 차가 바짝 지나가는 구간이 있었어요. 어머니는 "그래서 요즘은 장도 잘 안 간다"고 하셨지요. 부모님이 덜 걸으시는 까닭이 의지가 아니라 길에 있을 수도 있겠다는 생각이 들었습니다.

한눈에 보는 답부터 말씀드릴게요. 걷기 좋은 동네는 부모님이 더 많이 움직이시는 것과 관련이 있었어요. 60세 이상 어르신의 신체활동에 영향을 주는 요인을 다룬 연구들을 모아 본 큰 정리에서, 걷기 좋은 동네와 신체활동 사이의 좋은 관계를 보고한 연구 정리가 네 편 중 세 편이었어요[3]. 또 45세 이상 성인을 다룬 연구 23편을 살펴본 정리에서는 걷기 편한 보행로와 보기 좋은 거리가 몸 기능과 좋은 관계가 있었어요[4].

## 걷기 좋은 동네에 사시면 부모님이 정말 더 걸으실까요?

여러 연구를 보면 그런 경향이 있었어요. 어르신 신체활동 연구를 크게 정리한 연구에서는 1만 7천여 건의 기록을 살펴 연구 정리 11편, 300편이 넘는 원래 연구를 묶어 보았어요[3]. 그 결과 어르신 신체활동과 가장 꾸준히 관련이 있었던 요인은 걷기 좋은 동네, 나이, 성별, 그리고 운동을 함께하거나 응원해 주는 사람이었어요[3].

이 연구는 세계 여러 나라에서 어르신의 50%까지가 몸을 충분히 움직이지 못한다고 밝히며 시작해요[3]. 그만큼 "더 걸으세요"라는 말만으로는 바뀌기 어렵다는 뜻이기도 해요. 걷고 싶어지는 길, 그리고 같이 걸어 주는 사람이 함께 있을 때 걸음이 늘어날 수 있어요.

다만 한계도 있어요. 정리에 들어간 연구 가운데 오랜 기간 같은 사람을 따라간 연구는 6%뿐이었고, 76%는 본인이 직접 답한 활동량만 썼어요[3]. 그래서 "동네가 좋으면 반드시 더 걷는다"고 단정할 수는 없고, 관련이 있었다고까지만 말할 수 있어요.

## 어떤 길이 부모님 몸 기능과 관련이 있었을까요?

걷기 편한 보행로와 보기 좋은 거리였어요. 동네 환경을 아홉 가지로 나누어 살펴본 정리에서, 인도 같은 보행 시설, 그리고 거리의 아름다움이 몸 기능과 좋은 관계를 보였어요[4]. 여러 가게와 시설이 섞여 있는 정도, 범죄와 차로부터의 안전은 그보다 약한 근거가 있었어요[4].

몸 기능이란 계단을 오르고, 장바구니를 들고, 한참 서 있을 수 있는 힘처럼 혼자 생활하는 데 필요한 능력을 말해요. 즉 꽃이 놓인 골목, 끊기지 않는 인도처럼 걷고 싶은 길이 가까이 있는 것이 부모님의 평소 생활 힘과 함께 움직였다는 뜻이에요.

## 어르신에게 걷기 좋은 동네는 무엇이 다를까요?

젊은 사람에게 좋은 길과 어르신에게 좋은 길은 조금 달라요. 독일어로 된 측정 틀을 만든 연구에서는 전문가 20명에서 28명이 여러 차례 의견을 모아, 어르신에게 걷기 좋은 동네를 재는 지표 72개를 정했어요[6]. 지표는 길과 교통 시설, 가까운 곳에 갈 데와 만날 곳이 있는지, 그리고 보기 좋고 안심이 되는지의 세 갈래였어요[6].

그중 35개 지표는 어르신의 몸 상태에 따라 따로 보아야 한다고 했어요[6]. 같은 길이라도 튼튼한 분과 쉽게 지치는 분에게는 다르게 느껴진다는 뜻이에요. 쉬어 갈 의자 하나, 낮은 턱 하나가 부모님에게는 나서느냐 마느냐를 가를 수 있어요.

## 우리 동네가 걷기 불편하면 어떻게 할까요?

동네를 바꾸기 어렵다면 걷기 좋은 곳을 찾아 나서는 방법이 있어요. 한 연구 정리는 작은 시골 마을에서도 큰돈 들이지 않고 할 수 있는 방법으로 작은 보행 시설, 동네 공원, 함께 가꾸는 텃밭을 꼽았어요[5]. 집 근처 공원이나 텃밭처럼 가고 싶은 목적지가 있으면 걸음이 자연스럽게 생겨요.

권고량도 기억해 두면 좋아요. 세계보건기구는 65세 이상 어르신께 일주일에 중간 강도 유산소 활동 150~300분 이상을 권하고, 채우지 못하더라도 조금이라도 하는 것이 아무것도 하지 않는 것보다 낫다고 말해요[7]. 걷는 것은 운동이기 전에 세상과 다시 이어지는 문이에요. 문밖으로 나서고 싶은 길을 찾는 것이 첫걸음이에요.

## 자주 묻는 질문

**Q. 걷기 좋은 동네로 이사해야 부모님이 건강해지실까요?**
연구는 걷기 좋은 동네와 신체활동이 관련이 있었다고 말할 뿐, 이사가 건강을 바꾼다고까지 보여 주지는 않았어요[3]. 지금 동네에서 걷기 편한 길을 찾는 것부터 해 보셔도 좋아요.

**Q. 어떤 산책길을 고르면 좋을까요?**
보행로가 잘 이어지고 보기 좋은 길이 몸 기능과 좋은 관계를 보였어요[4]. 차와 떨어져 있고, 쉬어 갈 곳이 있고, 걷고 싶어지는 길을 고르시면 돼요.

**Q. 시골에 사시는 부모님은 어떻게 하나요?**
동네 공원이나 함께 가꾸는 텃밭처럼 비용이 적게 드는 방법이 걷기를 늘릴 가능성이 있다고 했어요[5]. 마을회관이나 텃밭까지 가는 길을 산책길로 삼아 보셔도 좋아요.

## 오늘 해 볼 작은 걸음

걷기 좋은 동네는 멀리 있지 않을 수도 있어요. 부모님과 이렇게 해 보세요.

- 다음에 부모님 댁에 가면 집에서 가게, 공원, 경로당까지 같이 걸어 보며 인도가 끊기는 곳과 쉬어 갈 곳 살펴보기
- 차가 덜 다니고 보기 좋은 길을 하나 골라 "우리 산책길"로 정해 두기
- 전화로 "오늘 그 길 걸으셨어요?" 대신 "이번 주말에 같이 걸어요" 한마디 건네기

sources.title: Association between neighborhood aesthetics and childhood obesity.
sources.journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
sources.text: The lack of neighbourhood aesthetics (e.g. public art and well-maintained properties) may reduce walkability in the neighbourhood and increase the risk of childhood obesity. In this study, a literature search was conducted in the Cochrane Library, PubMed and Web of Science for articles published before January 1, 2019 to analyse the associations between neighbourhood aesthetics and weight-related behaviours and outcomes among children and adolescents aged <18. One cohort study and 24 cross-sectional studies, conducted in 10 countries with a median sample size of 1124 were identified. Neighbourhood aesthetics was more commonly assessed by self-reported or parent-reported perceptions than objective measurements. Eighteen of the 25 included studies analysed physical activity (PA) as the outcome of interests, eight studies analysed active transport to school (ATS), and eight studies analysed weight status, including body mass index and overweight/obesity status. About two-thirds of studies reported non-significant associations when using PA and weight status as outcomes, and half of studies showed that neighbourhood aesthetics is associated with increased use of ATS. The rest of the studies reported mixed findings with slightly more studies showing neighbourhood aesthetics may promote PA or reduce weight. Better designed studies are necessary to achieve a robust understanding of this epidemiological relationship in the future.

sources.title: Walkability indices and childhood obesity: A review of epidemiologic evidence.
sources.journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
sources.text: The lack of an active neighbourhood living environment can impact community health to a great extent. One such impact manifests in walkability, a measure of urban design in connecting places and facilitating physical activity. Although a low level of walkability is generally considered to be a risk factor for childhood obesity, this association has not been established in obesity research. To further examine this association, we conducted a literature search on PubMed, Web of Science and Scopus for articles published until 31 December 2018. The included literature examined the association between measures of walkability (e.g., walkability score and walkability index) and weight-related behaviours and/or outcomes among children aged under 18 years. A total of 13 studies conducted in seven countries were identified, including 12 cross-sectional studies and one longitudinal study. The sample size ranged from 98 to 37 460, with a mean of 4971 ± 10 618, and the age of samples ranged from 2 to 18. Eight studies reported that a higher level of walkability was associated with active lifestyles and healthy weight status, which was not supported by five studies. In addition to reviewing the state-of-the-art of applications of walkability indices in childhood obesity studies, this study also provides guidance on when and how to use walkability indices in future obesity-related research.

sources.title: Determinants of physical activity in community-dwelling older adults: an umbrella review.
sources.journal: The international journal of behavioral nutrition and physical activity
sources.text: INTRODUCTION: Physical activity (PA) is critical for disease prevention and maintaining functional ability with aging. Despite this, as many as 50% of older adults in populations worldwide are considered insufficiently active. There is a recognized need to mobilize policies targeted toward modifiable determinants of healthy aging like PA. This umbrella review aimed to summarize the evidence for determinants of PA in community-dwelling older adults. METHODS: A research librarian searched six databases. Systematic and scoping reviews were included if they investigated community-dwelling people with a mean age of 60 + years and examined a relationship between a determinant and any type of PA. Two independent reviewers screened and extracted data from all reviews. JBI methodology and Critical Appraisal Checklist for Systematic Reviews and Research Syntheses were followed and information on the quality of the evidence was extracted. RESULTS: From 17,277 records screened,11 reviews representing > 300 unique primary papers were ultimately included. Only 6% of studies included in all reviews had longitudinal designs. Included studies used a large variety of PA measures, with 76% using only self-report, 15% using only direct measures (e.g., accelerometry), 3% using both types, and 6% with no outcome measure reported. Only four reviews provided a definition of PA and there was substantial inconsistency in the way PA was categorised. Community level influences, which only included the physical environment, were the most commonly assessed (6/11) with more than 70% of the summarized relationships demonstrating null associations. Three out of four reviews reported a positive relationship between walkability and PA in general community-dwelling older adults. There was also evidence supporting relationships between presence of social support for PA, younger age, and men having higher PA from a single systematic review. None of the included reviews assessed the quality of evidence but over 60% performed a risk of bias assessment. CONCLUSIONS: Walkability, age, gender, and social support for PA were the most supported PA determinants identified. Further research should focus on interpersonal and intrapersonal influences and incorporate direct measures of PA with clear operational definitions. There is a need for longitudinal study designs to further understand determinants of PA behaviour trajectories.

sources.title: Neighbourhood built environment and physical function among mid-to-older aged adults: A systematic review.
sources.text: This systematic review included 23 quantitative studies that estimated associations between aspects of the neighbourhood built environment and physical function among adults aged ≥45 years. Findings were analysed according to nine aspects of the neighbourhood built environment: walkability, residential density, street connectivity, land use mix, public transport, pedestrian infrastructure, aesthetics, safety and traffic. Evidence was found for a positive association of pedestrian infrastructure and aesthetics with physical function, while weaker evidence was found for land use mix, and safety from crime and traffic. There was an insufficient number of studies for walkability, residential density, street connectivity and access to public transport.

sources.title: Translating Urban Walkability Initiatives for Older Adults in Rural and Under-Resourced Communities.
sources.journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
sources.text: The built environment can promote physical activity in older adults by increasing neighborhood walkability. While efforts to increase walkability are common in urban communities, there is limited data related to effective implementation in rural communities. This is problematic, as older adults make up a significant portion of rural inhabitants and exhibit lower levels of physical activity. Translating lessons from urban strategies may be necessary to address this disparity. This review examines best practices from urban initiatives that can be implemented in rural, resource-limited communities. The review of the literature revealed that simple, built environment approaches to increase walkability include microscale and pop-up infrastructure, municipal parks, and community gardens, which can also increase physical activity in neighborhoods for urban older adults. These simple and cost-effective strategies suggest great potential for rural communities.

sources.title: A Framework for Measuring Neighborhood Walkability for Older Adults-A Delphi Consensus Study.
sources.journal: Journal of urban health : bulletin of the New York Academy of Medicine
sources.text: While mobility in older age is of crucial importance for health and well-being, it is worth noting that currently, there is no German language framework for measuring walkability for older adults that also considers the functional status of a person. Therefore, we combined the results of an expert workshop, a literature review, and a Delphi consensus survey. Through this, we identified and rated indicators relevant for walkability for older adults, additionally focusing on their functional status. The expert workshop and the review led to an extensive list of potential indicators, which we hope will be useful in future research. Those indicators were then adapted and rated in a three-stage Delphi expert survey. A fourth additional Delphi round was conducted to assess the relevance of each indicator for the different frailty levels, namely "robust," "pre-frail," and "frail." Between 20 and 28 experts participated in each round of the Delphi survey. The Delphi process resulted in a list of 72 indicators deemed relevant for walkability in older age groups, grouped into three main categories: "Built environment and transport infrastructure," "Accessibility and meeting places," and "Attractiveness and sense of security." For 35 of those indicators, it was suggested that functional status should be additionally considered. This framework represents a significant step forward in comprehensively covering indicators for subjective and objective walkability in older age, while also incorporating aspects of functioning relevant to older adults. It would be beneficial to test and apply the indicator set in a community setting.

sources.title: WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour (2020)
sources.text: 65세 이상 어르신 권고: 일주일에 중간 강도 유산소 신체활동 150~300분 이상, 또는 고강도 75~150분 이상. 중간 강도 이상의 근력 운동을 일주일에 2일 이상. 기능적 균형과 근력을 강조한 복합 신체활동을 일주일에 3일 이상(기능을 높이고 낙상을 막기 위해). 앉아 있는 시간을 줄이고 어떤 강도든 신체활동으로 바꾸는 것이 건강에 이롭다. 권고량을 채우지 못하더라도 조금이라도 하는 것이 아무것도 하지 않는 것보다 낫다.
